title: Repository Understanding & Task Scoping
description: Study map the codebase before editing, read local instructions and constraints, define acceptance criteria, and separate facts from hypotheses. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Map the codebase before editing
lessons.description: Trace the active route to its service and locate the tests that exercise it.
lessons.conceptOverview: Identify entry points, ownership boundaries, build commands and existing conventions before making a change. Search for the behavior and its callers rather than assuming the first similarly named file is authoritative.
lessons.whyItMatters: Edits should follow the active execution path.

lessons.title: Read local instructions and constraints
lessons.description: Find the source of truth and describe the regeneration path.
lessons.conceptOverview: Project instructions can define style, generated files and required checks. Reconcile them with the actual task and inspect nearby patterns so a change integrates with the repository.
lessons.whyItMatters: Generated output should be changed through its source when appropriate.

lessons.title: Define acceptance criteria
lessons.description: Write an acceptance case for the reported failure and one boundary case.
lessons.conceptOverview: Translate a request into observable behavior, edge cases and explicit scope. Concrete before-and-after examples reduce ambiguity and provide a basis for verification.
lessons.whyItMatters: Acceptance criteria should describe observable task behavior.

lessons.title: Separate facts from hypotheses
lessons.description: List the measurement that distinguishes network delay from rendering work.
lessons.conceptOverview: During investigation, distinguish observed failures from suspected causes. Gather targeted evidence before changing multiple layers, and keep hypotheses falsifiable.
lessons.whyItMatters: Diagnosis should follow evidence rather than the first plausible cause.
